<reason>A won by keeping the motion as written and crystallizing a cleaner vote: visibility can be sold, but working locks, the best available check, and real scam-help cannot be merchandised as perks. B had the sharper mechanisms—false halo, de facto ID pressure, flood risk, funding—but often answered gating with a subsidy story and recast the motion as mandatory ID plus unlimited concierge. A’s clipped R1 and weak “fix the interface” reply keep it competitive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure Qs plus R2: if a free-tier harasser can walk back in, the “working lock” is the door, not a perk; CON’s payment wall still faces the older user hit by one unpaid profile, not the predator.</best_rebuttal>
